what_they_do: Astrada runs an API that pulls real-time, structured transaction data straight from card networks and bank accounts, instead of the delayed, unstructured batch feeds finance platforms normally rely on. Expense management, travel, and ERP platforms plug into it to see spend on any card an employee uses, personal or corporate, not just cards the platform itself issued, and to auto-reconcile card transactions against bank settlements as they happen. It replaces the manual, days-later process of finance teams matching card statements to bank records line by line.
vertical: Fintech data infrastructure (spend management / finance ops)
theme_fit_rationale: Astrada's transaction API and auto-reconciliation product are the connective data layer for cross-system finance workflows (card networks, banks, ERPs, expense platforms), the exact close-reconciliation and AR/AP use case called out in Theme 2, and the company explicitly frames itself as infrastructure for 'autonomous finance.'

recent_signals.summary: Closed a $3.8M seed round co-led by Bain Capital Ventures, QED Investors, and Nyca Partners, with strategic participation from Mastercard and follow-on from existing investor Visa.

Seed announcement blog post: $750M+ in card spend and 3M+ transactions processed across all three major card networks since the 2024 launch; proceeds go toward product development (Auto-Reconciliation, Enrichment) and partnership expansion.

prior_insights: Last note on Astrada. I think the "bring your own card" approach is a really clean way to solve the visibility gap. Most expense platforms only see spend on cards they issue, which means almost half of what a company actually spends is invisible to them. Plugging directly into the card networks and delivering structured data at authorization gives platforms something they've never had before. $750M in card spend processed since launch is great early traction.
